approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples breeding parents from score quantiles, combines connected fragments and applies ordinary atom, bond and ring edits with its retained continuation rules; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection admit a fresh surplus pool. A narrow sulfur rule rejects new or multiplied disallowed signatures relative to the maximum count in the original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete earlier accepted archive represents molecules by counts of local environments and uses generalized Tanimoto covariance. Correlated posterior function draws choose each successive batch member while masking previously chosen identities. Actual accepted scores update the greedy survivor population and chronological prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Remove only sampled residual influence from successful allocation: select the highest original posterior mean at each available-mask step, keeping the original model, covariance, factorization and function draws as passive computations. This isolates whether sampled departures from the mean still contribute after sulfur admission changes the pool and ancestry. Current siblings replaced a mean path or residual law, removed multiplicity, or removed the entire successful selector; none isolates original residual presence on this gated Parent. Earlier mean-only controls on ungated Parents lost endpoint score and remain prior evidence. This is a changed-applicability contribution test, not a claim of a new performance gain.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is the unisolated dependence of productive exploration on original sampled residual departures after sulfur admission changed the available pool and later ancestry. Parent n-1744a1494180 completes all supplied summaries/run logs with macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917; its gain over n-62daf219c70a is only +0.0007834645552323346, with the negative seed-two cell retained. A read-only scan of all fifteen actual Parent task logs records 435 posterior pools and 4350 successful positions, 3763 strict same-mask mean losses, zero sampled-rule mismatches and zero maximum-mean ties. Stable top-mean allocation on those logged pools changes all 435 ordered batches, 433 selected sets and 4068 positions; these are decision comparisons without alternate oracle labels. Full current composite control n-605c7a785b51 loses -0.12818290031998167 and supports the joint selector only. Historical isolated mean-only n-299096e31fe7 loses -0.07686116167690966 against ungated n-62daf219c70a, although three endpoint cells improve and local beats increase. Current residual substitution n-6ebafca203bf loses -0.02971005981260903 despite more local beats and new productive cores, and changes residual variance/dependence rather than removing original residual presence. These concrete observations leave the exact gated constituent contribution unresolved; neither weaker selected-stream error nor novel/core/local-win counts establish endpoint benefit.
hypothesis: Remove only original sampled residual influence on successful pool allocation by choosing the maximum original count-GP posterior mean on each inherited available mask, resolving exact ties by the first pool index, while retaining full original covariance, Cholesky, normal-array consumption and correlated sampled arrays as passive computations with unchanged failure routing.

finding_summary.headline: Mean-only allocation loses 0.11632; sampled residuals contribute under the sulfur gate
finding_summary.insights: The loss cannot be explained by a missing intervention, absent natural choice exposure, altered original model arithmetic, broken accepted-feedback joins or a changed sulfur admission rule: those checks passed. Higher predicted means and lower error on the acquired stream did not preserve the best observed outcome. Selected-stream MSE was lower than Parent in all 15 cells, yet pair ordering and Spearman were worse in 14; the only favorable ranking cell was zaleplon seed 2. Those comparisons describe different adaptively acquired streams. On identical Child identities and labels, active and passive original-mean prediction/ranking contrasts are exactly zero. The narrower selected cores and the Molecular assessment's repetitive connected families are consistent with restricted exposure, while reactive attachments remain in both methods; they do not identify why residual sampling helped or establish chemical mediation. Lack of later breeding is also insufficient as a general explanation: 657 of 659 nonterminal parent-winning Child sources were actually drawn, versus 636 of 639 in Parent. However, 390 drawn Child winners had no productive direct accepted descendant, versus 343 in Parent. Each panel's 150 final-batch offspring remain censored. This answers the current gated residual-presence criterion as one total adaptive removal contrast. It does not establish constituent additivity, sulfur interaction, the value of covariance dependence, independent validation, a complete optimizer foundation or transfer from older ungated Parents; those questions remain open.
finding_summary.results: Every mean-only choice followed the original model mean, with no non-tied mean-loss decisions. The original sampled rule preferred a different identity at 3,958 of 4,350 actual mask positions. A separately masked replay changed all 435 batch orders and 434 selected sets; 2,731 actual accepted molecules were outside its sets. On these same Child pools, mean-only selection raised the average sum of ten predicted means from 3.16569 to 3.42482, lowered selected latent SD from 0.03059 to 0.01583, and raised count-Tanimoto redundancy from 0.58199 to 0.82801. The model uncertainty and original draws remained intact. All 15 task/seed evaluations completed. Macro score fell from 0.59645311 to 0.48013623, a loss of 0.11631688. Paired seed changes were −0.22680180, −0.03988971 and −0.08225913. Twelve task cells lost; median-2 seeds 0 and 2 and sitagliptin seed 1 improved. Local parent wins rose from 648 to 668, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.45530 to 0.37127 and mean offspring score from 0.37205 to 0.33081. Total incumbent gain fell from 5.81942 to 4.07466; new nonempty generic cores with a strict parent-beating member fell from 168 to 101. These complete, exposed results support positive conditional contribution of original sampled residual presence at the registered 0.002 scale.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with reactive attachments and limited productive scaffold change
molecular.overall_character: Current applicability: n-f04cec6ab705 versus complete code Parent n-1744a1494180, selected lineage L01, Research in Depth epoch 1, issued Search seeds 0/1/2, all five independent objectives, 300 accepted observations including ten common initial molecules, announced batch ten, greedy64 survivors, fresh full160 de novo pools, exact original-generating-parent per-signature sulfur maximum, disabled aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange, identical retained count posterior computations and original draws with only successful mean-based identity consumption changed. The exact full frozen applicability_conditions strings are preserved in support evidence.json; historical ungated or other Parent controls supply no new comparison cells here. All 30 Child/Parent task-seed trajectories and summaries, plus their complete diagnostic logs, were read; no path or pairing is missing. Each role has 4350 accepted offspring across its 15 cells, and all 290 offspring per cell have actual optimizer feedback. Across the Child accepted offspring, 668 strictly beat their best original generating parent, 566 tie and 3116 lose; Parent has 648, 186 and 3516. More local wins therefore coexist with Child macro endpoint 0.4801362322985727 versus Parent 0.59645311428869 and paired delta -0.11631688199011732. All endpoint signs, including improving cells, are retained per task. These are existing observed values; chemistry association does not assign a constituent contribution or activation result. Overall ring and aromatic content are rich, synthetic plausibility questionable, medicinal resemblance moderate and structural diversity narrow within streams. Exact identity turnover is much broader than core turnover. Child accepted molecules include 516 with O–O bonds and 641 with N–halogen bonds, versus Parent 128 and 786. These offline RDKit graph counts are distinct from digest SMILES-text rates. The sulfur gate has 69600 actual allowed pool candidates and 282 rejected candidates in Child, versus 69600 and 130 in Parent; all accepted Child/Parent molecules have zero positive gate differences, and no observed allowed candidate retains an outside-envelope centre. The rejected pools have no observed rewards. Permitted sulfur remains environment-dependent, and this sulfur-only rule admits N–halogen/peroxide liabilities. The generated/admitted pool is not the accepted scored stream: 69600 admitted pool candidates per role yield 4350 emitted/accepted molecules; invalid, duplicate and sulfur-rejected attempts remain in the full support denominators. Child logs record 434 changed passive-comparator batch sets out of 435 and 3958 same-mask differing choices out of 4350. Those passive choices have no labels or alternate ancestry; no reward, productive core or synthetic superiority is assigned to them. Actual initial sources, strict-beat sources, incumbent-gain sources and unsupported sources are recorded separately from generated candidates. Child has 659 supported offspring sources with a later chronological horizon, of which 657 are drawn and 267 have an actual productive direct accepted descendant; Parent has 639, 636 and 293. Child unsupported offspring sources with a later horizon number 3541, of which 2134 are drawn and 281 have a productive direct accepted descendant. The Child also has 674 unsupported offspring sources that never survive their birth batch; support keeps these separate from survivors that are never drawn. Of the 150 initial sources per role, only the 75 that reach a selectable menu are later drawn. These denominators describe actual accepted-source exposure and outcomes, not independent chemical effects. Sources with a later chronological horizon are used for draw/nonuse denominators; support additionally reconstructs each actual greedy-survivor batch and top-half selectable-parent opportunity, and reports birth-to-first-draw intervals. A later horizon is not necessarily an eligible parent draw. All final-batch births have no subsequent fit/draw; their actual feedback exists, so terminal censoring is not failed delivery. Direct edges can share a descendant across multiple original parents, and connected ancestry is counted separately rather than added as independent credit. Batch-frozen gain and sequential incumbent increments are separate in support; novelty uses the accepted archive before the batch, preserves within-batch repeated new cores, and excludes empty cores from nonempty novelty. Full absolute score distributions, parent deltas, explicitly defined chronological archive-horizon and crossover/mutation/mixed strata, born-survivor/non-survivor cohorts, unsupported-but-drawn and supported-but-undrawn cohorts, accepted descendant scores/edges and connected reachability are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/round-0028-slot-2/molecular/evidence.json. None establishes independent exploration, additive component value, chemical mediation or universal transfer.

Identity diversity mostly changes attachments on a shared core; three-digit score plateaus are not independent chemical discoveries.
missing_features: The connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl variation visible in Parent leaders is less broadly expressed: Child new generic cores have no accepted strict parent-beating member in any seed. This supports a missing productive scaffold-change capability, not a unique required pharmacophore.

Chemically conventional alternatives to N-halogen and hydrazino-amide/amidine attachment edits are underrepresented among the leaders; scores alone do not show which stable replacement would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the smaller decorated indole amidine with N–F and phenol scores 0.42762099872850584. The Br fragment scores 0, difluorobenzene 2.2064040954992307e-13, and the duplicated indole/anilide scores 2.523871379065681e-09. Thus the visible gradient supports retaining the connected indole/aryl polar linkage and a restricted substituent balance, while both severe fragmentation and oversized duplication are penalized. Many distinct N–halogen or halomethyl variants have exactly the same upper score; these plateaus cannot establish a reward for any one reactive attachment. Parent best examples include an aza-indole N-hydroxyamide and a pyridyl carbonyl/thione-linked indole, but one Parent leader itself contains N–F. Parent score superiority does not imply synthetic quality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Reobserved source n-f04cec6ab705 versus current complete Parent n-1744a1494180 under the frozen gated batch-ten, 300-observation Search panel. Child accepted graphs include 641 N–halogen-bearing molecules and 516 with O–O bonds, while every digest stereocentre counter is zero. Sulfur admission has no accepted positive signature difference, yet the non-sulfur reactive attachments remain. Some leaders score well with these attachments; this is chemical liability evidence, not proof of their score mechanism or that a blanket filter improves endpoints.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically conventional functional-group environments when useful cores are locally edited.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-agnostic functional-group-aware transformations that can produce stable alternative attachments while preserving connected rings and polar-group relationships. Treat peroxide length, nitrogen substitution and sulfur neighbor context explicitly. Compare accepted absolute outcomes and retained search exposure before attributing any advantage; avoid assuming a local valence envelope provides global feasibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This inherited Parent limitation is reobserved in the current Child under the same complete Search/profile conditions. Accepted leaders contain dense fused/bridged aza-dione closures and highly unsaturated small rings; all five Child digest stereocentre rates are 0.0. Rich ring-closure text is consistent with substantial rings, but it is not a strain, synthesis or configuration measurement. Parent high-score examples retain similar liabilities, so its superior endpoint is not a synthetic-quality baseline.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces valence-valid connected ring graphs without reliably establishing credible geometry or stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically credible ring-size, unsaturation and bridge-connectivity edits and preserve or resolve stereochemistry only where meaningful. Retain ring-rich alternatives and measure actual accepted scores; no missing specific stereoisomer or feasibility benefit is established by the present evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Current source n-f04cec6ab705 with complete current-Parent pairing at the frozen profile only. Child has 668 strict parent wins versus 648 in Parent but a lower absolute macro endpoint; some streams have no parent-beating member on any batch-new generic core. Most supported nonterminal sources are actually drawn, yet many have no productive direct accepted descendant. All terminal-batch births lack later opportunity and are censored; unsupported sources are drawn as well. Shared parentage and connected descendants are not independent credit or mediation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Identity turnover is substantially broader than productive core turnover, and local-win sources often fail to produce another improving accepted molecule.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs credible ways to reconnect scaffold topology and retain useful functional arrangements, with success measured on absolute accepted offspring, incumbent gains and later source/descendant use rather than novelty or win counts alone. Diagnose nonuse separately from unsuccessful reuse and preserve adverse seed cells before designing changes.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
